note: Officeholders and districts as listed by Citizens Count, the NH Secretary of State roster, Rockingham County and news coverage, checked Oct 23, 2026. Positions are the officials' own survey answers or quoted statements, with the year. Nothing here is characterized or scored.
ballot_note: All Rockingham County offices, the Executive Council, the State Senate and every State House seat are on the Tuesday, Nov 3, 2026 ballot, along with Governor, US Senate and US House. Results will replace the names below.

levels.title: Federal
levels.blurb: Two senators and one representative. Portsmouth is in New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District.

levels.title: State
levels.blurb: The Governor, your Executive Councilor (District 3), your State Senator (District 21), and the State House members for your ward.

levels.title: Rockingham County
levels.blurb: County government runs the jail, the sheriff's office, the county attorney (prosecutor), the nursing home and the registry of deeds. Its share of your tax bill is about 5%. All county offices are two-year terms, elected Nov 3, 2026.

massahos.name: Charles (Chuck) Massahos
massahos.status: Of Salem. First elected 2018, reelected since. The sheriff's office handles court security, prisoner transport, civil process and the county Drug Task Force. On the Nov 3 ballot.
positions: The office aims to be "a community-based police organization."
Plans to strengthen the Rockingham County Drug Task Force
Plans to expand active shooter training programs
massahos.caveat: The state Attorney General reviewed a claim that he improperly reduced a county employee's speeding ticket and found he had the discretion to do so.

conway.name: Patricia Conway
conway.status: The county's chief prosecutor. Handles felony cases from Portsmouth and 36 other towns, victim and witness services, and right-to-know requests. On the Nov 3 ballot.
positions: "provide professional and ethical prosecutorial services for the people of Rockingham County"
Justice for victims, less repeat offending
Stated goals include achieving justice for crime victims and reducing crime and repeat offending
conway.caveat: Party and first year in office are not stated on the office site; her campaign site blocks automated reading. Not characterized here.

coyle.name: Kate Coyle
coyle.status: Chair of the three-member board, which runs county operations, the budget, buildings and personnel. District 1 covers Portsmouth, Rye, New Castle, Greenland, Newington, Exeter, Hampton and seven other towns. On the Nov 3 ballot.
coyle.caveat: No position statements on record in the sources checked. The board posts its meeting minutes; the county does not publish per-commissioner votes in a structured form.

stacey.name: Cathy Ann Stacey
stacey.status: Records property deeds, mortgages and liens for the county. On the Nov 3 ballot.
stacey.caveat: Administrative office; no policy positions apply.
